candidate_048.name: execution-grounded critique trigger / reproduce-before-promote
candidate_048.mechanism: For computational-science claims that are executable, require at least one re-execution/reproduction or claim-linked counterfactual comparison before terminal scientific review. Treat discrepancies or execution failures as issue-ledger triggers, because critique generated from prose alone can miss defects that become visible only after running and comparing the underlying computation.
candidate_048.source: arXiv:2604.12198, Towards grounded autonomous research: an end-to-end LLM mini research loop on published computational physics, 2026-04-14
candidate_048.quantitative_evidence: Across 111 open-access computational-physics papers the agent raised 88 substantive critiques; 86/88 (97.7%) surfaced only after execution, with only one genuine reading-only catch among 111 papers (0.9%). The study reports roughly three-quarters of in-scope claims reproduced within 5% and a 12-paper independent-machine cross-check with overlapping critique categories on 7/12.
candidate_048.scope_guard: Observational phase attribution in a computational-physics reproduction loop, not a matched ablation proving that a mandatory reproduce-before-promote gate improves final scientific quality. Do not generalize the 97.7% number outside this corpus or to non-executable empirical science.
